To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a displacement vector model is a good choice to represent the respiratory motion of the lungs, and that the diaphragm can be used as reference for motion prediction.

a prediction framework for motion modeling is feasible, that the diaphragm position is a suitable motion parameter for prediction of the lungs motion, and that a displacement vector representation of motion is superior to a position vector representation.

the diaphragm can be used as a surrogate marker of the lungs, that the motion of the diaphragm and the lungs is highly correlated, and that motion prediction of the lungs based on the diaphragm is possible with an error of about 4 mm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of the lung motion based on statistical models, which can be used to reduce the uncertainties in the localization of organs and tumors during image guided interventions.
the development of a framework for statistical respiratory motion modeling, which can provide a prediction of the organ motion based on a statistical model.
the development of statistical motion models of the lungs and the diaphragm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the displacement vector-based representation is the best one, when the diaphragm position is known, but the other representations are better suited when the diaphragmatic motion is not available.
the prediction error of a displacement vector-based model is about 3.5 mm, which is a promising result for image-guided interventions on the thorax and upper abdomen.

, the displacement vector-based representation of the dynamic data can be used for statistical modeling and that the prediction framework can provide an efficient way for building a statistical breathing model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prediction of lung motion is possible, but it is not yet possible to predict lung motion without the knowledge of diaphragm motion.
a displacement vector based representation is a suitable representation for the statistical modeling of respiratory motion, if the diaphragm position can be measured with sufficient accuracy.

the presented framework can be applied for statistical modeling of respiratory organ motion and the displacement vector representation is a promising candidate for the dynamic data representation in such a model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the prediction framework for statistical respiratory motion modeling is a powerful and versatile tool, which can be used to predict organ displacements in the case that the diaphragm is used as a reference.

a statistical motion model based on a displacement vector representation of the dynamic image data, can be built with a high accuracy and can predict the motion of the lungs with a high accuracy as well.
a displacement vector representation is superior to other representations for motion model building and prediction, when the motion model is trained on data from the same patient.
